author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Build a repeatable PS2 graphics regression test scene
summary: Create a legal in-game checkpoint with fixed camera, inputs, settings, expected artifacts, timing window, and clean-save recovery so renderer, driver, and emulator updates can be judged against the same workload.
heroAlt: PCSX2 regression bisect diagram showing a known-good and known-bad build range

blocks.text: Select a scene that exposes multiple graphics paths

A useful regression checkpoint is short, deterministic, and visually rich. Prefer a route containing geometry, transparency, shadows, particles, HUD, a camera pan, and a transition, while avoiding random weather or enemy behavior. Use a normal in-game save so the scene can survive emulator-state incompatibility.
A save state alone is not a durable test fixture. Core changes can invalidate it or preserve stale renderer state, creating a false regression.

items: A private normal save immediately before the route.
Exact serial, revision, personal image hash, and emulator build.
Renderer, driver, resolution, accuracy, aspect, and patch inventory.
A written input sequence or controller recording permitted for private QA.
Expected screenshots and frame-time window from the known-good run.

blocks.text: Create a checkpoint another clean run can reproduce

items: 1. Cold-boot the known-good build and load the normal in-game save.
2. Define a start marker visible in the scene and a fixed route under thirty seconds.
3. Record camera movement and inputs with timing relative to the marker.
4. Capture expected frames for shadow, transparency, HUD, edge geometry, and transition points.
5. Record warm frame-time range separately from visual pass/fail evidence.
6. Close the app, reboot, and reproduce the route from the same normal save.
7. Repeat once on the candidate driver or emulator build with no setting changes.
8. Version the fixture notes when game progression or settings must change.

blocks.text: Determinism reduces noise between builds. Separate visual expectations from performance expectations because a frame can be correct but slow, or fast because an effect vanished. A normal save plus written route remains useful after save-state formats change. Record tolerances explicitly: which pixels or layers must match exactly, which animation differences are acceptable, and how many consecutive runs may leave the timing envelope before the candidate is classified as a regression.
The checkpoint is ready only when an independent cold run reaches the same evidence.

items: Start marker, camera path, and capture moments can be repeated.
Expected graphics layers appear in the same order.
Normal save recovery works without an emulator state.
Settings and build identifiers are complete.
Known-good runs stay within the documented visual and timing envelope.
Random weather changes the effect: choose a controlled scene.
Enemy AI moves the camera or particles unpredictably: shorten or relocate the route.
Only a save state reaches the fault: build a normal-save path.
The baseline itself changes across cold runs: isolate cache or lifecycle state first.

blocks.text: Retire fixtures that cannot stay deterministic
Keep the original normal save and known-good captures, discard the unreliable input route, and choose a new checkpoint. Do not edit expected images to make a noisy scene appear stable.

Do not place game saves, screenshots, dumps, or disc-derived data into the public Hub repository unless distribution is clearly permitted. Public instructions can describe the method without bundling the fixture.
